title: Skin fragility & dermatoporosis
summary: Actinic purpura, thin skin, skin tears and stellate pseudoscars — protect fragile skin and review anticoagulants/steroids carefully.

glance.think: Painless purple patches on thin sun-damaged forearms after minimal trauma in an older person.
glance.engine: UV and age destroy dermal support around vessels → easy shear bleeding; advanced form is dermatoporosis with skin tears.
glance.backbone: Reassure, protect (sleeves, pad furniture), daily emollient and sun protection; medication review with the prescriber.
glance.never_miss: Palpable purpura, non-exposed-site bruising, mucosal bleeding or safeguarding patterns — investigate / escalate.

what: **Actinic (senile/Bateman) purpura** is benign purple-red ecchymoses on thin sun-damaged forearms and hands after minimal trauma. **Dermatoporosis** describes chronic cutaneous insufficiency — atrophy, purpura, stellate pseudoscars and **skin tears**.

list: Chronic UV + intrinsic ageing → dermal collagen/elastin loss; vessels rupture with minor shear.
Aggravators: anticoagulants, antiplatelets, topical/oral/inhaled **corticosteroids**, SSRIs, fish oil/ginkgo/high-dose vitamin E.
Platelets and clotting are usually normal in classic actinic purpura.
Irregular dark-red/purple patches 1–5 cm on extensor forearms and dorsal hands; fade to brown haemosiderin.
Thin translucent wrinkled skin; stellate pseudoscars; skin tears from shear/adhesive dressings.

diagnosis: Clinical at typical sites. Investigate FBC/clotting/LFTs (± INR) if purpura is on covered sites, palpable, with mucosal bleeding, systemic symptoms, new anticoagulant, or unexpected INR rise. Consider elder abuse if history/pattern mismatch.

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Grip marks, multiple ages of bruise

list: Protect: long sleeves, tubular forearm protectors, pad furniture, careful carer transfers; avoid harsh adhesives.
Medication review with the GP — **never stop an anticoagulant solely for actinic purpura** without discussion.
Skin tears: gently approximate, non-adherent dressings, tetanus status; refer complex wounds.

red_flags: Palpable purpura or systemic vasculitis signs.
Large unexplained bruises with rising INR.
pearls: Actinic purpura is a counselling and protection problem more than a cream problem.
Inhaled as well as topical steroids can contribute — ask.
Document skin-tear classification if using local wound pathways.
